patch_description:
The current program's extra RX input layer (alongside RY) adds parameters without clear benefit and matched the weaker 90-param design. The strongest prior program (0.53) used: a single RY orbit-shared sign decoder, CRY line entanglers (endpoint→edge, pair→center, center→edge broadcast), and RY+RX orbit-shared readouts — 12 params/block, 72 total.

I restore that proven compact structure but add one improvement: instead of having both `ry_corner_out` AND `rx_corner_out` as separate full readout layers, I keep the RY+RX readout (which the best program used) but tie the decoder to be RY-only (removing the wasteful RX input layer in the current code). This removes the 3 extra RX-input params (rx_corner_in/rx_edge_in/rx_center_in) per block that the current 0.44 program introduced, bringing us back to the efficient 12 params/block × 6 = 72 total configuration that scored 0.53.

This is parameter-efficient (fewer params, lower depth) and matches the architecture that demonstrably generalized best.
